messages:
erin_customer: Hey team — after we moved to Dedicated + VPC with the customer's L7 edge, our clients intermittently get 401s. Happens more when session affinity cookie rotates or traffic goes to different backend. Repro attached below.

alice_support: Thanks, can you paste the curl you used and response headers? Also send a request_id if you have one.

erin_customer: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted-token>' https://api.customer.example/v1/generate
* Connected to api.customer.example (10.10.10.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.customer.example
> Authorization: Bearer VALIDTOKEN
> 
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"
< x-request-id: abc-123-def
< set-cookie: AWSALB=some-alb-cookie; Path=/; HttpOnly

erin_customer: note: if we hit the same pod repeatedly it's fine; when the cookie causes a different backend (sticky cookie change?) it fails.

alice_support: interesting — from the response headers I see an ALB cookie. Are you using an internal HAProxy/edge that rewrites headers into cookies or vice-versa?

bob_eng: look at the ingress stack notes: customer runs NLB -> internal HAProxy (sticky) -> istio ingressgateway -> our dedicated gw. We saw a few configs where HAProxy rewrites Authorization into X-Auth-Session and sets a cookie, and Istio ext_authz policy is configured to sanitize headers.

bob_eng: paste of problematic HAProxy snippet we found in the customer's config:
```
frontend https-in
  bind *:443
  http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Proto https if { ssl_fc }
  # custom: move bearer to cookie for legacy backend
  http-request add-header Set-Cookie "edge_auth=%[req.hdr(Authorization),regsub(^Bearer ,,)]" if { hdr(Authorization) -m found }
  http-request del-header Authorization if { hdr(Authorization) -m found }
```

bob_eng: and their Istio ext_authz filter (simplified):
```yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: strip-auth-if-cookie
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: internal-legacy
  rules:
  - when:
    - key: request.headers[Cookie]
      values: ["edge_auth"]
    action: DENY_WITHOUT_AUTH_HEADER # pseudo-rule used in their stack (custom ext_authz)
```

carla_infra: ugh — so HAProxy strips the Authorization header and encodes it in a cookie, then the Istio policy sees the cookie and refuses requests that don't have the Authorization header. The header never gets to our dedicated gateway in that path.

dave_sre: quick repro I ran from a test VM inside the VPC: direct to pod IP (bypass HAProxy/ALB) with same token -> 200. Through HAProxy -> 401. So HAProxy is doing the mutation.

dave_sre: curl direct: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer VALIDTOKEN' http://10.244.1.5:8080/health` -> 200

dave_sre: curl via HAProxy: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer VALIDTOKEN' https://edge.example/health -v` -> 401 and response contains `set-cookie: edge_auth=VALIDTOKEN` and no Authorization in request reached the pod.

alice_support: possible quick mitigations for customer so they stop seeing 401s:
- stop HAProxy from deleting Authorization (remove `http-request del-header Authorization`).
- OR change HAProxy so it forwards a preserved header, e.g. `X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer <token>` and update ext_authz to accept that header.
- OR adjust Istio ext_authz / AuthorizationPolicy to look up `edge_auth` cookie and treat it as valid (less ideal).

bob_eng: long-term fix: ensure any L7 edge in front of Istio/dedicated GW does NOT mutate Authorization -> cookie. We can also add gate-side support behind a feature flag: allow `X-Forwarded-Authorization` to be trusted when originating from customer VPC ranges and mTLS is present. That's a code + rigorous config change.

erin_customer: can we get a quick config snippet to send to the customer's infra team? They asked for a minimal change.

alice_support: send them this HAProxy-safe snippet to preserve header instead of swapping to cookie:
```
# preserve Authorization and set a forward header for legacy backends
http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Authorization %[req.hdr(Authorization)] if { hdr(Authorization) -m found }
# remove the header only if explicitly required by legacy backend (avoid doing this)
# http-request del-header Authorization if { hdr(Authorization) -m found }
```

alice_support: and a minimal Istio ext_authz tweak (pseudo):
```yaml
# ext_authz: accept X-Forwarded-Authorization when present and trusted
# make sure to only trust from internal subnet / mTLS sources
matchers:
  - any:
    - header: { name: Authorization }
    - header: { name: X-Forwarded-Authorization }
```

carla_infra: also told them to check ALB cookie config. If ALB rebalances, sticky cookie semantics can flip backend which surfaces the header mutation more often.

dave_sre: filed infra ticket to add a temporary popup rule on our dedicated gw to accept X-Forwarded-Authorization from that customer's VPC until they deploy HAProxy patch. Ticket RED-4521.

authbot: automated-scan: found 3 other customers with similar HAProxy cookie->header rewrites in last 90 days. Flagging for infra docs.

bob_eng: i'll draft an internal KB that describes this HAProxy -> Istio interaction and recommended patterns (preserve Authorization, or if you must use cookies, have your ext_authz validate cookie contents and re-create Authorization at edge).

erin_customer: thanks all — i'll forward the HAProxy snippets to the customer's infra team. we'll let you know after they patch. :thumbsup:

alice_support: mark follow-up: check RED-4521, confirm whether gateway temporary rule was applied, and verify customer reports 200s again.

erin_customer: update: customer patched HAProxy in staging (removed del-header and added X-Forwarded-Authorization) — staging now shows 200s. They'll schedule prod change next week.

alice_support: great. closing for now, reopen if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
